presentation_revision_history.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: one square premium painterly mythology encyclopedia illustration. Subject: SWAN MAIDEN in the whole-swan transformation from Herman Hofberg's Swedish Fairy Tales (1890), Blekinge tale. ONE wholly swan-bodied magical woman in animal form standing on a quiet Scandinavian lakeshore at dusk, about to leave. Natural white swan plumage, one swan head and long graceful curved neck, one natural bill with black base and orange bill, exactly TWO feathered wings slightly spread, exactly TWO webbed black feet clearly apart on shore, one coherent bird body and short feathered tail. No human face, human torso, human arms, costume, crowns, jewel or invented hybrid anatomy. The entire swan from wing tips and neck to both feet and tail fits frame with ample margin. Peaceful wistful distant gaze, proud regained freedom and gentle fairy-tale melancholy rather than demonic hostility. Soft warm dusk lake reflection, deep forest green background, walnut shore and nuanced gold light, premium detailed naturalistic oil-painted texture. Only this individual bird, no other swans or people. No text, watermark, borders or gore. Depict an actual source-attested animal metamorphosis; do not substitute a woman wearing feather robe.

visual_review.notes: Individually inspected via view_image: one natural swan head/long neck, orange-black bill, exactly two feathered wings, two distinct black webbed feet, one white-feathered avian body and tail; all tips/feet visible inside square frame. No human face/body, costume or invented hybrid anatomy. Quiet lakeside sunset and poised wistful bird retain graceful maiden-in-animal-form tale aura. Explicitly based on Hofberg's whole-swan metamorphosis.

root_visual_review.notes: Individually viewed original. One complete white swan with two spread wings, two webbed feet and one feathered tail. No human features. Wistful lakeside sunset aura fits documented whole-swan maiden transformation.
